# RenderCamera <img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14">

<div align="center">

[Command Index](Command-Index) · [Blitz3D](Blitz3D) · [World](Blitz3D-World)

</div>


```blitzbasic
RenderCamera:Void camera:Int32, tween:Float32=1
```

| Parameter | Mode | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `camera` | In | Int32 | required | Camera handle. |
| `tween` | In | Float32 | `1` | As for RenderWorld: 0 draws what [CaptureWorld](CaptureWorld) saw, 1 (the default) where everything is now. |

## Description

<img class="product" src="media/bl-20x14.png" alt="BlitzLLVM" title="BlitzLLVM" width="20" height="14"> This command does not exist in the original Blitz products. BlitzLLVM adds it.

Draws the world as one camera sees it, and no other camera. The picture goes into the camera's own buffer ([SetCameraBuffer](SetCameraBuffer)) or, if it has none, into the current buffer, inside the camera's viewport and with its clear settings and fog. This is a BlitzLLVM extension.

A camera with [CameraProjMode](CameraProjMode) 0 draws nothing. A hidden camera is still drawn, so a program can hide the cameras it wants to draw itself and leave the others to [RenderWorld](RenderWorld).

Several RenderCamera calls in one frame are one frame: movies and the sounds of entities are brought up to date by the first call after a [Flip](Flip), and [TrisRendered](TrisRendered) counts the triangles of all of them. RenderWorld always starts a new count.

## Examples

```blitzbasic
Graphics3D 320, 240, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
cube = CreateCube()
main = CreateCamera()
PositionEntity main, 0, 0, -5
map = CreateCamera()
CameraViewport map, 220, 10, 90, 90
PositionEntity map, 0, 20, 0
RotateEntity map, 90, 0, 0
HideEntity map ; RenderWorld leaves it alone.

RenderWorld
Text 10, 10, "Drawn by RenderWorld"
RenderCamera map ; The map is drawn on top of the text.
Flip
```
